title: Compact routing hotpath by introducing decision-shield worker and migrating fallback plugins
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: The smart routing hotpath currently performs policy evaluation, fallback invocation, telemetry enrichment, and regional affinity resolution on a single synchronous execution path. This has produced contention (global mutexes), unpredictable p99s, and a high engineering surface area when adding new fallback plugins. Goal: Reduce hotpath surface area by extracting a compact, fast decision path (decision-shield) that only performs deterministic routing choices. Non-deterministic work (fallback plugin execution, heavy telemetry enrichment, slow dependency calls) will be migrated to a separate, controlled worker/executor with backpressure and feature flags. This reduces lock contention, simplifies reasoning for p50/p95, and creates a stable plugin migration strategy for legacy fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Decision-shield implementation accepts routing requests and returns a deterministic route decision within < 1.2x current p50 for the same input in local perf tests
All legacy fallback plugins are migrated to the fallback-worker and invoked asynchronously; hotpath no longer blocks on plugin execution
Global routing mutexes removed or limited to < 10ms critical sections; documented in code comments
End-to-end integration test coverage added for fallbacks and regional failover scenarios
Canary rollout configured (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on p99 or error rate regressions
Console dashboard tile showing hotpath latency and fallback worker queue depth created and linked
design_decisions: Introduce a single-threaded decision-shield fast path that performs: deserialize request, policy evaluation (compiled rules), route selection, and minimal token for telemetry. All other work moves out-of-band.

Fallback plugins run in a separate worker pool (fallback-worker) with a bounded queue and SLA-based admission; fallback results are written into a short-lived KV cache so API callers can read consistent state.
Use a feature flag (ff-routing-decision-shield) to gate the new path and allow gradual traffic migration.
Upgrade proto definitions for route evaluation to proto3.25 to support compact enums and reduce serialization cost (see dependency upgrades).
Prefer optimistic reads of regional affinity from a local read-copy structure to avoid global locks; fall back to strong read only on miss.
updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff - scoped MVP and agreed on decision-shield name. PM accepted low customer impact. (Maya Chen)

2026-03-03: Prototype: extracted policy-eval into a small in-process library; microbench shows ~18% p50 improvement for synthetic workloads. Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/421 (WIP). (Liam O'Connor)

2026-03-06: Design review with infra and runtime teams. Concern raised about falling back to synchronous behavior when fallback-worker is saturated. Action: add admission controller and soft-fail path to force fallback to next compatible region. (Priya Patel)
2026-03-09: Dependency upgrade plan: protobuf 3.21 -> 3.25 and grpc to 1.55. Verified local build matrix. Need ops approval for runtime-2.5 cut. (Maya Chen)

2026-03-11: Integration tests added for regional failover + fallback queue backpressure. Observed a p99 regression in one test due to a locking edge-case; temporary mitigation added: short-circuit lock on hot-signature. (Liam O'Connor)
2026-03-12: Prepared canary config and dashboard. Ready to enable feature flag in staging for 10% traffic. (Maya Chen)
risks: If fallback-worker queue saturates, callers may experience degraded completeness of fallback execution. Mitigation: admission controller with graceful degradation and cached last-good fallback results.
Dependency upgrades (protobuf/grpc) may interact with other services; must coordinate with infra and run e2e across Dedicated and Private deployments.
Telemetry gaps during migration; must ensure we do not lose critical signals used by billing and SLAs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for decision-shield policy evaluator and proto contracts
Integration tests: regional failover + fallback-worker fallback delivery + KV cache coherence
Load tests: 2000 RPS simulation comparing old hotpath vs decision-shield path; measure p50/p95/p99 and CPU
Chaos tests: simulate fallback-worker slowdowns and verify graceful degradation
Canary in staging: enable ff-routing-decision-shield for 10% staging traffic for 48h and monitor dashboards
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge behind feature flag; run e2e in staging for 72h
Stage 2: Canary 1% production for 2 hours, monitor p99 and error rates
Stage 3: Expand to 5% for 6 hours, then 25% for 12 hours with auto-rollback triggers
Stage 4: Full enablement at 100% after 48h stable metrics
Fallback rollback: flip ff-routing-decision-shield off will fall back to legacy hotpath; run a postmortem if triggered
metrics: Hotpath p50/p95/p99 (routing service) - target: p50 <= 1.1x current p50, p99 improved or no worse than current
Fallback-worker queue depth and rejection rate - target: < 0.5% rejections at normal traffic
CPU utilization for routing service - target: -15% median compared to baseline in synthetic load
Error rate for route decisions and downstream retries - target: no increase
Observed rollback triggers set: p99 +20% or error rate +100% for 5m
notes: Follow-ups: extract shared policy-compiler into runtime-common package (follow-up ENG-? to be created)
Plan a cross-team upgrade window for protobuf/grpc during runtime-2.5 cut; inform Dedicated account owners one week ahead
Document migration guide for third-party fallback plugins and provide adapter shim for compatibility
Post-merge action: schedule 2h pairing session for on-call rotation to review first canary rollout
